threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 243 bus is a reliable way to get around. Locals know it’s just a suggestion, not a schedule.
Caught a night bus from Brixton, saw a guy serenading a cat on the seat. The driver just shook his head, but the cat seemed to enjoy it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a guy selling homemade falafel from a stand on the corner while debating the latest BVG strike with his customers. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop open 24/7, where the line is always long, even at 4 AM. It's the pulse of the night here.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local when they know which taco truck has the best al pastor after a late night out—hint: it’s not the one on 24th.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw someone feeding a pigeon in Civic Center while waiting for the bus. Muni was late again, but the bird seemed unfazed. Classic San Francisco moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but locals know it’s the vibrant plazas and quirky boutiques that make it home.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still take photos of every building with a colorful door, like it's a rare sight. Locals just walk right past them.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus is the best way to get around—everyone else knows it's the overground or a bike, especially with these tube strikes.
Last week on the N35, a guy serenaded the whole bus with old reggae tunes. Felt like I was in a mini concert at 2 AM, all of us swaying along.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard a saxophonist playing incredible jazz at 2 AM while waiting for the night bus on Karl-Marx-Straße. Pure Neukölln magic.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can overhear conversations about the best Döner spots while waiting for the U-Bahn at midnight. The city's late-night food culture is a unique blend of old and new.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local when they know the difference between a burrito from La Taqueria and one from Chipotle without a second thought.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy trying to teach his dog how to ride the bus at Civic Center. The pup wasn't having it, just plopped down in the aisle. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just Gaudí and art. They miss how locals actually prefer the no-frills bars where the wines flow and the gossip's even better.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the ‘Si, un café’ at local cafes; it's the stunned look when they realize it’s not just coffee.
